task: Add SubWorkflowNode type with warm pre-instantiation pool, isolated child execution context, interrupt/resume support across parent-child boundary, and UI-configurable pool and nesting depth settings

key_reasoning.reason: New SubWorkflowNode, greenfield pool manager, background pool-watcher, and substantial modifications to workflow_execution_service.py, checkpoint_saver.py, workflow.py, workflow_config.py, workflow_execution.py — 4+ new abstractions introduced across a redesigned orchestration subsystem; bumped from XL to XXL because base_node.py (base class for all nodes) and checkpoint_saver.py (all workflow state) are core shared utilities

Three novel sub-problems with no codebase precedent: (1) parent-child LangGraph checkpoint coordination with risk of silent data loss on incorrect resume, (2) greenfield pool lifecycle with concurrency hazards — stale instances, double-checkout, pool drain on config change, (3) extended interrupt/resume mechanism originally designed for single-level workflows; bumped from XL to XXL for performance optimization as a primary requirement and mandatory Alembic migrations

Conservative source-file count: 10 modified (workflow.py, checkpoint_saver.py, base_node.py, workflow_execution.py, workflow_config.py, workflow_models.py, workflow_executions.py router, workflow_execution_service.py, workflow_update_output_service.py, config.py) + 4 new (sub_workflow_node.py, pool_manager.py, 2 migration files) + approximately 5 new test files; bumped from XL to XXL after the data migration red flag

All five primary layers are touched: API (workflow_executions.py router — interrupt/resume path), Service (workflow_execution_service.py, workflow_update_output_service.py), Workflow/Orchestration (workflow.py, checkpoint_saver.py, new sub_workflow_node.py), DB-Persistence (two schema migrations, new model columns in workflow_config and workflow_execution), Configuration (config.py global defaults); bumped from XL to XXL for the significant DB schema changes across two tables

High-level requirements are well-specified (isolated context, explicit output only, warm pool with background watcher, UI-configurable pool and nesting depth, before-interrupt support), but multiple architectural decisions remain open: LangGraph checkpoint namespace strategy for parent-child thread hierarchy, pool concurrency model (async locking, starvation handling), background watcher registration lifecycle (FastAPI lifespan vs BackgroundTasks), and whether pool registry requires persistence or is purely in-memory

split_recommendation: This XL ticket (30/36) should be decomposed before planning begins. Splitting strategy by dependency order: Story 1 (M) — SubWorkflowNode class: new node type inheriting base_node.py, thin invocation interface delegating to service layer, unit tests validating isolated context (sub-workflow state must not leak into parent). Story 2 (M) — Workflow pool manager and background watcher: greenfield pool lifecycle service (create, checkout, return, refill, drain), async background watcher registered via FastAPI lifespan, in-memory per-workflow registry, concurrency-safe checkout. Story 3 (M) — DB schema and configuration: Alembic migrations for workflow_config (pool_enabled, pool_size, max_nesting_level) and workflow_execution (parent_execution_id, nesting_depth), config.py global defaults, model field additions and API exposure. Story 4 (L) — Interrupt and resume across sub-workflow boundary: checkpoint_saver.py parent-child namespace coordination, workflow_executions.py resume path for sub-workflow suspension points, nesting depth enforcement and circular call guard in workflow_execution_service.py. Story 5 (S) — Output isolation enforcement: workflow_update_output_service.py rule that only the sub-workflow explicit output surfaces to the parent context, integration test for state non-leakage.
